name: Quanzhou: Emporium of the World in Song-Yuan China
description: Quanzhou, on China's southeastern coast in Fujian, was one of the world's busiest ports from the 10th to 14th centuries, known to Arab traders as Zayton. Marco Polo and Ibn Battuta both marvelled at it. The inscribed sites include the 11th-century Qingjing Mosque, one of China's earliest, along with Islamic tombs, old stone docks, ancient bridges, pagodas and the remains of kilns and ironworks.
